question: Which of the following is/are termed as nucleons?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both protons and neutrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nucleons** are particles found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The term "nucleons" encompasses both **protons** and **neutrons**.
 
• Protons are positively charged particles, while neutrons are neutral, having no electrical charge.
 
• Both protons and neutrons contribute to the atomic mass of an element.
 
• Nucleons are bound together in the nucleus by the strong nuclear force, which is one of the four fundamental forces of nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrons**:

 
 
• Electrons are negatively charged particles that orbit the nucleus of an atom in electron shells.
 
• Unlike protons and neutrons, electrons do not reside in the nucleus.
 
• The number of electrons in an atom determines its chemical properties and reactivity.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Number**:
 
 
• The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of protons in the nucleus of its atoms.
 
• The atomic number defines the identity of an element and its position in the periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes**:
 
 
• Isotopes are variants of a particular chemical element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
 
• Isotopes of an element exhibit similar chemical behavior but can have different physical properties, such as different mass numbers and stability.
 
 
 
• **Strong Nuclear Force**:
 
 
• The strong nuclear force is the force that holds protons and neutrons together in the nucleus.
 
• It is the strongest of the four fundamental forces but operates only over very short distances, on the order of a few femtometers (1 femtometer = 10^-15 meters).
 
• This force is essential for the stability of atomic nuclei.
